themes_detail.label: Public Safety/Order Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints surged to 13 THIS WEEK vs. a baseline of 1.6 per week (up 700%), and Public Urination complaints hit 13 last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (up 550%), suggesting a rapid deterioration in street-level order and public conduct enforcement in Far Rockaway over the past 7 days.
evidence: Non-Emergency Police Matter: 13 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.34, 700% spike)
Urinating in Public: 13 complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.1, 550% spike)
Both represent statistically anomalous spikes with z-scores above 6.0, indicating genuine systemic change rather than noise
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and local precinct about staffing, enforcement priorities, and whether complaints reflect actual incidents or perception shifts
Canvass residents and business owners on 5th Ave/Central Ave corridor about whether they've observed increased street disorder, panhandling, or public conduct violations

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 7 days, complaints about Dangling Street Signs jumped to 11 vs. baseline of 2.0 per week (up 450%), Damaged Trees spiked to 9 vs. baseline of 1.6 (up 454%), and Real Time Enforcement issues hit 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 baseline (up 700%), indicating accelerating neglect of public infrastructure across the district.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling: 11 complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.43, 450% spike)
Damaged Tree: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.05, 454% spike)
Real Time Enforcement (traffic): 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42, 700% spike)
reporting_angles: Walk the district to visually document dangling/missing street signs and damaged trees; photograph evidence and geolocate clusters
Request DOT and Parks maintenance schedules to determine if budget cuts or staffing shortages are driving deferred maintenance

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk/Curb Conditions Deteriorating
themes_detail.summary: Curb Condition complaints hit 3 last week vs. baseline of 0.2 per week (up 1100%), and Street Sweeping Complaints also spiked to 3 vs. baseline of 0.2 (up 1100%), suggesting a two-week trend of sidewalk and curb neglect that may reflect contracted sanitation service failures.
evidence: Curb Condition: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
Street Sweeping Complaint: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
Concurrent timing suggests systemic rather than isolated issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation (DSNY) to review street sweeping schedules and contractor performance in CD 414 over the past 3 weeks
Photograph streets near beaches and transit hubs to document litter, debris, and curb deterioration; compare to adjacent districts

themes_detail.label: Obstruction Complaints Persist
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 10 three weeks ago vs. baseline of 3.4 per week (up 196%, z-score: 6.68), suggesting a sustained multi-week pattern of blocked sidewalks, storefronts, or public right-of-way that may reflect vendor enforcement or construction interference.
evidence: Obstruction: 10 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.68, 196% spike)
Timing suggests this spike may be receding but warrants follow-up to confirm if issue has resolved
reporting_angles: Request 311 detail data to identify specific locations of obstruction complaints (street vendor concentrations, construction zones)
Interview NYPD and DOT enforcement teams about whether complaint spike corresponds to vendor crackdowns or active construction projects

themes_detail.label: Chronic Housing/Heating System Issues
themes_detail.summary: Heat/Hot Water complaints remain the highest-volume complaint type with 1,406 reports over 90 days, and Plumbing complaints total 414 (14% of heat complaints), together comprising a multi-month systemic housing quality issue that warrants investigation into landlord compliance and enforcement gaps.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water: 1,406 complaints over 90 days (15.6 per day average), largest complaint category in district
Plumbing: 414 complaints over 90 days, strongly correlated with heating system failures
Pattern reflects seasonal winter demand but also indicates persistent enforcement/repair gaps
reporting_angles: Identify and profile the 10-15 buildings with most repeat heat complaints; interview tenants about landlord responsiveness and HPD enforcement timelines
Obtain HPD violation and hearing data for CD 414 to determine whether heat violations result in meaningful penalties or are cyclically dismissed
